name: Korea B-2 Tourist Visa
description: Everything about Korea's B-2 Tourist Visa: visa-free entry for 106 countries, with 67 exempted from K-ETA requirements through 2026, application process for non-exempt nationalities, documents, and FAQ. Updated for 2026.
tagline: Short-term stays for tourism and business
keyRequirement: Valid passport from visa-exempt country (90 days) or visa application for non-exempt countries
targetAudience: Digital nomads on short exploratory visits
Business travelers attending meetings or conferences
Those scouting Korea before applying for a long-term visa

eligibility.label: Visa-exempt entry available for 106 countries (67 K-ETA exempt through 2026)
eligibility.description: Citizens of visa-exempt countries may enter Korea for up to 90 days without a visa. As of 2026, nationals from 106 countries have visa-free access to Korea for tourism. Additionally, 67 countries are currently exempt from K-ETA (Korea Electronic Travel Authorization) requirements through December 31, 2026. Check the Korea Immigration Service website for the current list of visa-exempt countries and K-ETA requirements.
tips: Some nationalities receive less than 90 days visa-free — verify your specific allowance
After December 31, 2026, K-ETA may be required for some nationalities — confirm K-ETA eligibility before travel

eligibility.label: Visa application required for non-exempt nationalities
eligibility.description: Citizens of countries not on the visa-exempt list must apply for a B-2 visa at a Korean embassy or consulate before travel.

eligibility.label: Valid passport for the duration of stay
eligibility.description: Passport must be valid for the duration of your intended stay. While there is no official 6-month rule for Korea, some airlines may enforce their own validity requirements — check with your carrier before travel.

eligibility.label: No employment or paid work in Korea
eligibility.description: B-2 holders are not authorized to engage in any employment, freelancing, or paid activities in Korea.

eligibility.label: Proof of return or onward travel
eligibility.description: Immigration officers may request proof of a return or onward flight when entering Korea.

duration.extension: Up to 90 days total (extension possible at immigration office)
duration.maxTotalDetail: 90 days per entry for visa-free nationals. 30–90 days per visa grant depending on nationality.

fees.applicationDetail: Varies by nationality. Typically ₩50,000–120,000 for a single-entry visa.
fees.notes: Visa-free entry has no application fee. Visa fees vary by nationality and number of entries (single, double, multiple). Check your nearest Korean embassy for exact fees.

documents.name: Valid Passport
documents.description: Must be valid for the duration of your stay with at least 2 blank pages. Some airlines may require 6+ months validity — check with your carrier.

documents.name: Visa Application Form
documents.description: Completed visa application form (only for non-exempt nationalities applying at embassy)

documents.name: Return or Onward Flight Ticket
documents.description: Confirmed booking showing departure from Korea within the permitted stay period

documents.name: Proof of Accommodation
documents.description: Hotel booking confirmation, Airbnb reservation, or invitation letter from a host in Korea

documents.name: Proof of Financial Means
documents.description: Bank statement or credit card statement showing sufficient funds for the duration of stay (no fixed minimum, but ₩2,000,000-4,000,000 recommended for a 90-day stay)
tips: Recent bank statement (within 1 month)
Show enough funds to cover accommodation and daily expenses

documents.name: Travel Itinerary
documents.description: Brief description of travel plans in Korea (some embassies require this)

applicationSteps.title: Check Visa-Free Status
applicationSteps.description: Verify whether your nationality is on Korea's visa-exempt list. Citizens of 106 countries can enter without a visa for up to 90 days. Additionally, verify if your country is exempted from K-ETA requirements (67 countries through December 31, 2026). Check the Korea Immigration Service or visa.go.kr website for current information.
tips: Visa-exempt periods vary by country (some get 30 or 60 days, not 90)
K-ETA exemption status expires December 31, 2026 — after that date, K-ETA may be required
The visa-exempt list is updated periodically — verify before travel

applicationSteps.title: Prepare Documents (If Visa Required)
applicationSteps.description: If your country is not visa-exempt, gather all required documents for the visa application at a Korean embassy or consulate.
tips: Check your specific embassy's requirements — they may differ slightly
Some embassies require appointment booking in advance

applicationSteps.title: Apply at Korean Embassy (If Visa Required)
applicationSteps.description: Submit your visa application at the Korean embassy or consulate in your country of residence. Some embassies accept applications by mail.
tips: Apply at least 2-4 weeks before your travel date
Keep copies of all submitted documents

applicationSteps.title: Enter Korea
applicationSteps.description: Upon arrival, present your passport (and visa if applicable) at immigration. Immigration officers may ask about the purpose and duration of your visit. Have your return ticket and accommodation proof accessible.
tips: Fill out the arrival card on the plane
Have accommodation address written in Korean if possible
Immigration officers may deny entry if they suspect you intend to work or overstay — be prepared to show return tickets and financial proof

applicationSteps.title: Register if Staying 90+ Days
applicationSteps.description: If you plan to stay for 90 days or receive an extension, you must register at the local immigration office within 90 days of arrival to obtain an Alien Registration Card (ARC).
tips: ARC is required for opening a bank account, getting a phone plan, etc.
Book an appointment on HiKorea before visiting the immigration office

processingTime.governmentReviewDetail: Visa-free entry is instant at port of entry. Visa applications take 1–2 weeks.
processingTime.notes: Processing times for visa applications vary by embassy, nationality, and season. During peak travel seasons, processing may take longer. Visa-free entry is processed at the airport or port upon arrival.

restrictions: No employment of any kind in Korea
No paid activities or business operations in Korea
Remote work for foreign employers is technically a gray area — B-2 does not explicitly authorize it
No employment of any kind is permitted on B-2 status — violations can lead to deportation and re-entry bans
workPermission.notes: The B-2 visa is strictly for tourism, transit, and short-term business activities (meetings, conferences). It does not authorize any form of employment. Digital nomads working remotely for foreign companies on a B-2 operate in a legal gray area. For authorized remote work, consider the F-1-D Digital Nomad Visa.

faqs.question: Can I work remotely on a B-2 tourist visa?
faqs.answer: The B-2 visa does not explicitly authorize remote work. While some digital nomads do work remotely during tourist visits, this is a legal gray area. Korea introduced the F-1-D Digital Nomad Visa specifically for remote workers. For stays where you intend to work remotely, the F-1-D provides clear legal authorization.

faqs.question: Can I extend my B-2 stay beyond 90 days?
faqs.answer: Extensions are possible in limited circumstances by applying at a local immigration office before your permitted stay expires. Extension is not guaranteed and is granted at the discretion of the immigration officer. Overstaying is a serious violation that can result in fines, deportation, and re-entry bans.

faqs.question: Can I switch from B-2 to F-1-D (Digital Nomad Visa) while in Korea?
faqs.answer: According to published immigration procedures, a change of status from B-2 to F-1-D may be possible at the local immigration office, provided you meet all F-1-D requirements (income ₩88,000,000+, remote employment, health insurance). However, not all status changes are guaranteed — check with the immigration office or HiKorea portal for current procedures.

faqs.question: What happens if I overstay my B-2 visa?
faqs.answer: Overstaying is a violation of Korean immigration law. Consequences may include: fines (up to ₩20,000,000), detention, deportation, and re-entry bans (1-10 years depending on the duration of overstay). Always leave before your permitted stay expires or apply for an extension in advance.

faqs.question: Do I need travel insurance for a B-2 entry?
faqs.answer: Travel insurance is not a published requirement for B-2 visa-free entry, but it is strongly recommended. Medical costs in Korea can be significant for uninsured visitors. Some embassies may require proof of insurance for visa applications.

faqs.question: Can I re-enter Korea immediately after my 90-day visa-free stay?
faqs.answer: There is no explicit published rule requiring a specific waiting period between visa-free entries. However, immigration officers have discretion to deny entry if they suspect someone is using repeated tourist entries to live in Korea. Frequent back-to-back entries may raise questions at immigration.

faqs.question: Can I open a bank account on a B-2 visa?
faqs.answer: Opening a bank account as a short-term visitor on B-2 status is generally difficult. Most Korean banks require an Alien Registration Card (ARC), which is typically issued only for stays of 90 days or longer. Some banks may offer limited accounts for tourists, but this varies by institution.

tips: Check visa-free status before booking flights — not all countries get 90 days
Have your return ticket and accommodation details ready for immigration
Download the HiKorea app for immigration-related information and appointments
T-money card is essential for public transportation — buy one at the airport
Keep a copy of your passport and entry stamp on your phone
If scouting Korea for a longer stay, use the B-2 period to research neighborhoods and coworking spaces
warnings: Overstaying even by 1 day is recorded and may affect future visa applications to Korea and other countries

communityTips.tip: Always double-check the visa-free period for your nationality. I'm from Brazil and only got 90 days, but my friend from the Philippines only got 59 days under a special arrangement.
Had a smooth entry at Incheon. Officer asked where I was staying and how long. Had my hotel booking on my phone and was through in 2 minutes.
Successfully changed status from B-2 to F-1-D at Seoul Immigration Office (Mokdong). Took about 3 weeks. Make sure you have all F-1-D documents ready before applying.

If you're from a visa-exempt country, you may need a K-ETA (Korea Electronic Travel Authorization) before boarding your flight. Check if your country requires it — some nationalities are exempt from K-ETA too.

pathsTo.name: Digital Nomad Visa
pathsTo.requirements: Remote employment with a foreign company and annual income of ₩88,000,000+ (GNI × 2). Must have health insurance covering Korea.
pathsTo.notes: For B-2 holders who want to legally work remotely in Korea. A change of status from B-2 to F-1-D may be possible at the local immigration office without leaving the country. Verify current procedures on HiKorea.
